standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Used at the first step of the counted proof (line 15383)
standard_prerequisites.use: Represents an associated prime by an element whose annihilator it is.

standard_prerequisites.name: The submodule of elements killed by a fixed element
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows that multiplying by a suitable element outside the associated prime places the witness inside the previous step of the filtration.

core_obligations: Induct on the length of the filtration and take a witness element m whose annihilator is an associated prime p (proof lines 15382-15383).
If m already lies in the penultimate submodule, apply the induction hypothesis; otherwise m maps to a nonzero element of the last quotient, forcing p contained in p_n (proof lines 15384-15386).

If the containment is strict, multiply m by an element of p_n outside p: the annihilator stays p and the product falls into the penultimate submodule, so the induction hypothesis applies again (proof lines 15387-15389).
proof_roadmap: Induct on the length of the filtration, reducing to the last quotient (proof lines 15382-15386).
Force the witness down one step by multiplying with an element of the last prime outside the associated prime (proof lines 15387-15390).
difficulty_reason: Given a filtration of M whose successive quotients are of the form R modulo a prime, the lemma states that every associated prime of M occurs among the primes attached to the filtration (statement lines 15369-15379). The proof does not invoke the theory of primary decomposition, which is not yet available at that point: it inducts on the length of the filtration, and in the critical case where the witness element does not already lie in the penultimate submodule it multiplies the witness by an element of the last prime outside the associated prime, an operation that preserves the annihilator while pushing the element one step down the filtration (proof lines 15381-15390). That pushing-down trick is the content of the argument. H2.
